title: Cues and the plan you make beforehand
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What is the cue that tells you a habit is about to start?

Jose summarized the chapter: with enough practice you pick up on the cues that predict certain outcomes. Relevant cues in a situation are the foundation of every habit. You do not always know what tipped you off, such as when you are hungry and grab something to eat.

He said the subconscious can overtake the conscious, and the relationship works the other way as well: you can consciously affect the subconscious by bringing the cues to light. Behavior change starts with this awareness.
A student said: pointing and calling works because by verbalizing it and saying it aloud you reinforce it and make yourself more aware.
Jose said that this brings it from the non-conscious to the conscious level, and you need a technique that works for you, but you have to pick one.
He said the book calls another technique an implementation intention: a plan you make beforehand about when and where to act. When X arises, I will perform Y.
A student said: it is being conscious and intentional and not just going through the motions. Another said: not leaving it up to chance.
Write one if-then for a habit you want: when X arises, I will do Y.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a cue you notice before a habit starts.
Write one way to make it conscious: say it aloud, write it, point at it.
Write an if-then for a habit you want.
Write when and where it will happen.
Write what you will do the first time you miss it.

check.q: What did Jose say behavior change starts with?
What did a student say pointing and calling does?
choices: Makes you more aware by saying it aloud
A plan beforehand about when and where to act

recap: Notice the cue. Make it conscious. Plan the if-then.
